scenes.say: On 3 November, America votes.
scenes.speak: On the third of November, America votes.

scenes.say: And Donald Trump's next two years hang on the result.
These are the US midterms, and they matter to India too.
scenes.title: The US midterms, explained

scenes.say: First, how American power is split.
Three branches: the President, Congress, and the courts.
scenes.title: Three branches

scenes.say: The President is elected separately from Congress.
Congress has two chambers: the House and the Senate.
The House has 435 members, elected every 2 years.
scenes.speak: The House has four hundred and thirty-five members, elected every two years.
scenes.label: House members · 2-year terms

scenes.say: Seats follow population, so California and Texas get far more than Wyoming or Iowa.
The Senate has 100 members: 2 per state, for 6 years.
scenes.speak: The Senate has one hundred members: two per state, for six years.
scenes.label: Senators · 2 per state · 6-year terms

scenes.say: Big or small, every state gets two.
A law must pass both chambers before the President signs it.
scenes.title: Both chambers must agree

scenes.say: Each chamber has its own powers.
scenes.title: Split powers

scenes.say: So lose either one, and the President's agenda can stall.
Now, the midterms. They come exactly halfway through a President's four-year term.
All 435 House seats are up, and about a third of the Senate: 33 or 34 seats.
scenes.speak: All four hundred and thirty-five House seats are up, and about a third of the Senate: thirty-three or thirty-four seats.
scenes.title: 3 November 2026

scenes.say: It's widely seen as a verdict on the President.
Parties pick candidates in primaries, and every state sets its own voting rules.
scenes.title: 50 states, 50 rulebooks

scenes.say: First past the post: the most votes wins the seat.
Local, state and federal races share one ballot, so no two voters get the same one.
By post, early, or on the day. Results can take days.
So what does 2026 look like?
scenes.speak: So what does twenty twenty-six look like?

scenes.say: History punishes the President's party.
Over the last 23 midterms, it lost an average of 27 House seats, and 3 in the Senate.
scenes.speak: Over the last twenty-three midterms, it lost an average of twenty-seven House seats, and three in the Senate.
scenes.label: Average House seats lost by the President's party, last 23 midterms

scenes.say: In the Senate, Republicans lead 53 to 47.
scenes.speak: In the Senate, Republicans lead fifty-three to forty-seven.

scenes.say: Democrats need to gain 4 seats, with toss-ups in Texas, Maine, Ohio and Alaska.
scenes.speak: Democrats need to gain four seats, with toss-ups in Texas, Maine, Ohio and Alaska.

scenes.say: In the House, the Republican majority is fragile.
And polls give Democrats a real path back.
Voters are judging a busy second term.
scenes.title: Trump's second term

scenes.say: His DOGE cost-cutting drive removed about 2,64,000 federal jobs.
scenes.speak: His doge cost-cutting drive removed about two lakh sixty-four thousand federal jobs.
scenes.label: Federal jobs cut by the Department of Government Efficiency

scenes.say: Core inflation is back up to 2.6 per cent.
scenes.speak: Core inflation is back up to two point six per cent.
scenes.label: US core inflation

scenes.say: The Iran war has disrupted energy through the Strait of Hormuz.
US petrol prices peaked at 4.50 dollars a gallon.
scenes.speak: US petrol prices peaked at four dollars fifty a gallon.
scenes.label: Peak US price, a gallon of petrol

scenes.say: And tariffs: 10 per cent on all imports, 125 per cent on Chinese goods.
scenes.speak: And tariffs: ten per cent on all imports, a hundred and twenty-five per cent on Chinese goods.
scenes.title: By executive order

scenes.say: Mass deportations hit Supreme Court limits, but legal immigration and asylum were curtailed.
So, what could happen? A Republican win frees Trump's hand.
A Democratic House means gridlock, and oversight.
A big Democratic win could revive impeachment. But removal needs two-thirds of the Senate.
And for India, the stakes are real.
Congress controls foreign trade and budgets.
In September 2025, Washington put a 100,000 dollar fee on new H-1B visa applications.
scenes.speak: In September twenty twenty-five, Washington put a hundred thousand dollar fee on new H one B visa applications.
scenes.label: Fee on new H-1B applications, from September 2025

scenes.say: Indians get more than 70 per cent of all H-1B approvals.
scenes.speak: Indians get more than seventy per cent of all H one B approvals.
scenes.title: Indians' share of H-1B approvals

scenes.say: That hit India's 200 billion dollar IT export industry, and Indian student numbers fell sharply.
scenes.speak: That hit India's two hundred billion dollar I T export industry, and Indian student numbers fell sharply.

scenes.say: On trade, in 2025, Washington put a 50 per cent tariff on Indian goods, over Russian oil.
scenes.speak: On trade, in twenty twenty-five, Washington put a fifty per cent tariff on Indian goods, over Russian oil.
scenes.label: US tariff on Indian goods, 2025

scenes.say: In early 2026, it was cut to an interim 18 per cent, with conditions.
scenes.speak: In early twenty twenty-six, it was cut to an interim eighteen per cent, with conditions.

scenes.say: On defence technology, ties have deepened under TRUST, to counter China's grip on chips.
A Democratic House could scrutinise Trump's tariffs and his Middle East interventions.
That may bring Indian exporters some relief.
But neither party is keen to tear down protectionism.
American supply chains come first, whoever wins.
